source.body:
# China's optics makers say AI orders are booked into 2028

**The bottom line:** China's optical-module chain sent one message in a flood of filings. Orders are full, the 1.6T (1.6 terabit-per-second) generation is ramping, and big overseas customers are now giving demand guidance for 2028. Memory is the other pressure point: AI datacenters are absorbing DRAM supply, and phone buyers are paying for it. Beijing's chip ambitions also got fresh fuel from Cambricon's results, DeepSeek's reported record fundraise and a new five-year informatisation plan.

## Optical modules: full order books and longer visibility

Innolight (300308.SZ / 3308.HK), the world's largest maker of the optical transceivers that link AI servers, said orders from its main overseas customers run through 2027. Some key accounts have given 2028 demand guidance ([HKEX](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/1023/2026102300380.pdf)). First-half revenue was CNY 41.78bn, up 182.5%, and net profit was CNY 13.65bn, up 241.7%. The company described pricing as "healthy" and competition as "orderly." It plans to cancel 5.65mn repurchased shares rather than use them for staff incentives ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/300308/AN202610231830833072.html)). Next-generation formats, NPO (near-packaged optics) and XPO, will "gradually release."

Its closest rival, Eoptolink (300502.SZ), said 1.6T modules have entered a sustained ramp with shipments accelerating ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/300502/AN202610231830831587.html)). It also approved a RMB 800mn–1bn buyback ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/300502/AN202610231830831590.html)). Accelink (002281.SZ) reported "ample" orders and no adverse change in trends ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/002281/AN202610231830830889.html)).

The read-through runs upstream to the component makers:

- **Sourcetech (688498.SH)**, which makes the laser chips inside transceivers, guided Q3 revenue up 265–293% and net profit up 579–660%. A second fab phase should add capacity around the turn of the year ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688498/AN202610231830832769.html)).
- **Lianxun Instruments (688808.SH)** tests 800G and 1.6T modules. It forecast Q3 profit up roughly 1,900–2,100% and says it is global number two in 1.6T core test gear ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688808/AN202610231830834114.html)).
- **TFC Optical (300394.SZ)**, a component supplier, reported H1 net profit of RMB 1.2bn on RMB 2.83bn revenue and said its co-packaged optics (CPO) parts are in stable mass production. Its new incentive plan targets net profit up 700% by 2029 versus 2025 ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/300394/AN202610231830833517.html)).

Capital is following. Unlisted Nazhen Technology says its 2027 indium phosphide laser-chip capacity, more than 100mn units, is already covered by orders ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2513186?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). Shijia Photonics (688313.SH) is seeking up to RMB 2.8bn for chip and interconnect capacity, and itself flags the risk of a shift to silicon photonics and CPO ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688313/AN202610231830848648.html)). Langte Intelligent (300916.SZ), a newcomer to optics, is paying ¥663mn for 51% of a passive-optics maker ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2513851?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).

The 2028 guidance supports the view that hyperscaler capex runs well beyond 2026. The risk is the classic one: a wave of new capacity arriving in 2027 just as CPO starts displacing pluggable modules. Watch whether leaders' "orderly pricing" survives that supply.

## Memory squeeze reaches consumers

A Caixin investigation shows the AI memory crunch now hitting phone shelves ([Caixin Global](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-10-23/in-depth-chinas-smartphones-get-pricier-as-ai-strains-chip-supply-102496477.html)). Price increases before China's National Day included:

- Xiaomi's 18 Pro, up 1,000 yuan
- Huawei's Mate 90, up nearly 28%
- the 2TB iPhone 18 Pro Max, up 3,500 yuan

TrendForce data cited in the piece show server DRAM contract prices rose about 64% in H2 2025, with a roughly 270% cumulative increase projected for 2026. Qualcomm's China chairman said he had never seen memory prices rise 4–5x in a year and expects high prices to persist through 2027. Memory made up nearly 60% of the bill of materials for sub-$400 phones in Q1. Demand is cracking: China shipments fell 4.3% in Q2, the fifth straight quarterly decline.

The article frames this as good for memory makers and bad for low-end handset brands, with scale players best placed. Supplier filings back it up. Baiwei Storage (688525.SH), a Shenzhen memory-module maker, said DRAM and NAND prices rose "significantly" in 2026 and proposed another buyback ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688525/AN202610231830847055.html)). Giantec (688123.SH), which makes the SPD chips on DDR5 modules, grew Q3 revenue 26% as SOCAMM2/LPCAMM2 modules launched. Its chips for CXL memory modules, which let servers pool memory, are now in customer validation ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688123/AN202610231830847992.html)).

China's DRAM champion CXMT voiced "firm confidence" in long-term demand ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610233906520425.html)). Caixin profiled Micron (MU) CEO Sanjay Mehrotra's push into high-bandwidth memory, the stacked DRAM used beside AI accelerators ([Caixin](https://database.caixin.com/2026-10-23/102496333.html)).

## China's AI chips, models and five-year plan

Cambricon (688256.SH), China's best-known listed AI-accelerator designer, more than doubled Q3 revenue to 3.53bn yuan (+104%). Net profit was 1.40bn yuan (+148%) ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688256/AN202610231830847887.html)). Rival GPU maker MetaX (688802.SH) set incentive targets of 60bn yuan revenue in 2027 and 300bn yuan cumulative over 2027–29 ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688802/AN202610231830849193.html)). These are internal hurdles, not guidance, but they show how much domestic substitution management expects.

DeepSeek reportedly closed a round of about 100bn yuan (~$15bn), a Chinese AI record. CATL and Tencent led, with chip-linked funds also participating ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniwfmnk5005978.d.html)). The headline of that report says 10bn, so treat the exact size as unconfirmed.

DeepSeek also open-sourced DeepInfer, the inference framework it uses to serve its own models. DeepInfer runs on both Nvidia GPUs and Huawei's Ascend 950 ([Caixin](https://www.caixin.com/2026-10-23/102496505.html)). That matters for Huawei's ecosystem: software that runs on either chip lowers the cost of switching away from Nvidia. Huawei separately raised a CNY 15bn offshore syndicated loan, its first in six years ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniweywq5020293.d.html)).

Policy points the same way. The 2026–2030 Informatisation Plan calls for:

- more advanced-node manufacturing capacity
- high-performance AI chips
- 3D integration and photonics-electronics convergence
- humanoid robots and quantum computing

([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniwffek8270214.d.html), [CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2513725?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). Shanghai targets 85% AI penetration in industry by 2028, with subsidies of up to 30% on rented compute ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610233906136377.html)). These are demand-side tailwinds for domestic chips and cloud.

## Datacenter boards and power

High-end circuit boards remain a bottleneck. Shengyi Electronics (688183.SH) guided nine-month profit up 68–75%. It cited growing orders for AI-server and 800G/1.6T switch boards and a "breakthrough" in 1.6T optical-module boards ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688183/AN202610231830847403.html)). Victory Giant (300476.SZ), a key Nvidia board supplier, said some customers have released demand through 2027–28 ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniweqhs8199552.d.html)).

Power is next. Megmeet (002851.SZ) showed a liquid-cooled 800V DC power platform with Nvidia at OCP, built into Nvidia's MGX server ecosystem. It also debuted a solid-state transformer module ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610233906214393.html)). Battery maker XiongTao (002733.SZ) wants to move RMB 336mn from a stalled lithium-battery plant into a RMB 1.5bn AI-datacenter power-supply project. Shareholders vote on 11 November ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/002733/AN202610231830848099.html)). Datacenter operator Runze (300442.SZ) is taking RMB 4bn from a China Eximbank unit for an AI infrastructure project ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniwffen5024680.d.html)), a sign of state-linked money backing compute buildouts.

## Materials and equipment

China Northern Rare Earth (600111.SH), the world's largest light rare-earth producer, grew Q3 net profit 161% on higher prices and volumes ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniweywn8173442.d.html)). That is consistent with tight magnet supply. In the US, the Department of Energy designated helium, essential for chip fabs, as a critical mineral ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniwfruh5124819.d.html)).

Japan's September chip-equipment orders rose 48.2% year on year ([Wallstreetcn](https://wallstreetcn.com/livenews/3184259)). That is a supportive data point for toolmakers such as Tokyo Electron (8035.T). Quartz Pure Materials (603688.SH), which makes high-purity quartz for fabs, credited semiconductor sales for a 46% Q3 profit gain ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610233906242523.html)).

## What to watch

- **Optics pricing into 2027:** watch Innolight's and Eoptolink's full Q3 reports for gross margins, and whether new laser-chip capacity from Sourcetech, Nazhen and Shijia tightens or loosens component supply.
- **DeepSeek round:** confirmation of the final size, and whether DeepInfer drives measurable Ascend adoption.
- **Memory contract prices:** whether Q4 DRAM quotes keep rising and how far handset demand weakens.
- **Shareholder votes:** XiongTao on 11 November and MetaX on 9 November.
- **Follow-on measures:** detailed rules under the five-year informatisation plan, especially any advanced-node manufacturing support.

## AI (19)

🔴 **[10-23 21:46 Beijing] Chinese state office issues guidance on AI development to foster employment-friendly economic growth**  
China's State Council Office (国办) issued "Opinion on Adapting to AI Technology Development and Assisting in Building an Employment-Friendly Development Model" (关于适应人工智能技术发展助力构建就业友好型发展方式的意见), aiming to expand new employment opportunities in emerging AI fields.  
_News · CLS · [Source](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2514013?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)_

🔴 **[10-23 19:20 Beijing] DeepSeek completes approximately 10 billion yuan funding round, record for China AI**  
DeepSeek closed ~100 billion yuan (~15 billion USD) Series funding round, setting record for single-round China AI fundraise. Funding target raised from 80 billion to 100 billion yuan. Existing investors CATL (宁德时代) and Tencent lead round; IDG, Enlighten (砺思), Shouxiang (拾象) continue. New industrial-capital investors: Lenovo-backed Junlian Capital (君聯), Gigadevice-backed Shixi Capital (石溪), Geely auto fund, Zhongxin Juhe (中芯聚源), Hengdian Capital (横店资本). Investment rationale: large-model development now primarily engineering problem; core barriers are training datasets and compute. DeepSeek required prospective investors to commit data and business-collaboration support; industrial investors with deep resource networks secured larger allocations (e.g., Hengdian).  
_News · Sina · DeepSeek · [Source](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniwfmnk5005978.d.html)_

🔴 **[10-23 17:55 Beijing] Runze Technology: subsidiary Hebei Runlan to receive RMB 4 billion strategic investment from China Eximbank for AI project**  
Runze Technology (300442.SZ) announces its wholly-owned subsidiary Hebei Runlan will receive RMB 4 billion strategic investment from China Export-Import Bank's subsidiary Jinyinxinjin in exchange for 144 million yuan increase in registered capital. Post-investment, Runze's stake in Hebei Runlan will decrease from 100% to 63.89%, though it remains controlled subsidiary. Funds earmarked for AI infrastructure project construction. Runlan plans further strategic investor refinancing up to RMB 2.8 billion at same valuation.  
_News · Sina · Runze Technology (300442.SZ) · [Source](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniwffen5024680.d.html)_

**[10-23 20:42 Beijing] China MIIT: prioritise AI+Software initiative, support intelligent-agent software, boost AI compute supply efficiency**  
Industrial and Information Technology Ministry (MIIT) held meeting in Hangzhou on advancing IT industry to strengthen advanced manufacturing. Meeting emphasised deepening IT's role in industrial development and seizing strategic initiative in digital-intelligent transformation. Key actions: reinforce tech autonomy (open-source ecosystems, baseline software, IP); intensify AI+Software initiative, support intelligent-agent software, implement industrial-data foundation action, build high-quality sector datasets, optimise government AI open-source community, improve intelligent-compute supply; deepen fusion initiatives via two-layer integration, scenario cultivation, industrial-internet platforms, intelligent industrial-sector products and solutions, manufacturer digitisation-transformation service providers. Strengthen element safeguards: industrial-software and industrial-data standardisation committees, trustworthy digital-tech standards, talent pipelines, international cooperation.  
_News · CLS · [Source](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2513945?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)_

**[10-23 17:01 Beijing] State Council affirms AI job creation; encourages eastern regions to deploy AI core industry**  
The State Council Office issued guidance on adapting to AI development and building employment-friendly growth models. The guidance deploys six priorities with 18 main tasks: (1) strengthening AI's job creation effects by expanding new AI employment spaces, cultivating SME job stabilization and expansion, developing new employment modes and occupations; (2) building employment-friendly AI upgrade pathways by exploring AI applications in traditional sectors and establishing AI application employment risk assessment mechanisms; (3) enhancing workers' digital skills and employment capacity through AI talent training; (4) advancing high-quality employment services using AI to improve policy implementation; (5) improving labor rights protection and social security systems for the AI era; and (6) strengthening AI employment monitoring, research, and risk response. The guidance specifically encourages eastern regions to deploy AI core industries and guides central and western regions to develop data annotation and smart terminal manufacturing in their supply chains.  
_News · CLS · [Source](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2513620?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)_

**[10-23 16:47 Beijing] Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing launches AI and Semiconductor indices**  
Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited announced the launch of two new indices: the HKEx AI Index and HKEx Semiconductor Index. The HKEx AI Index tracks 40 Hong Kong-listed companies highly related to the AI industry chain, covering five layers of the AI ecosystem architecture including chip design, data centers, AI infrastructure, AI models, and software and physical applications. The HKEx Semiconductor Index tracks 30 of the largest semiconductor-related companies listed in Hong Kong. The indices provide investors with benchmarks to capture opportunities from AI and semiconductor technology themes. Hong Kong Exchanges also authorized Nanyuan Asset Management to launch an ETF tracking the HKEx AI Index on mainland China's exchanges.  
_News · CLS · Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing · [Source](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2513592?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)_
